/-! ## The packaged chart module structure: scalar towers and the RE-0 bridge -/

section Packaged

variable [Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V]

/-- `IsScalarTower k Γ(X, V) F(W)` for any `W ≤ V`: the coefficient action of the
packaging factors through the structure map `k → Γ(X, V)`. -/
lemma isScalarTower_coeff
    (hq : ∀ {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)),
      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hW r s = gluedQsmul k U g hW r s)
    {W : X.Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) :
    letI : Module Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) :=
      Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, V) := (X.overAlgebraMap k V).toAlgebra
    IsScalarTower k Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) := by
  letI : Module Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) :=
    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV
  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, V) := (X.overAlgebraMap k V).toAlgebra
  refine IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun c m => ?_
  change Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV (X.overAlgebraMap k V c) m
    = c • m
  rw [hq hWV (X.overAlgebraMap k V c) m]
  exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap k U g hWV c m

/-- The map from the quotient of `M` by submodule `p` to the quotient of `M₂` by submodule `q` along
`f : M → M₂` is linear. -/
def mapQ (f : M →ₛₗ[τ₁₂] M₂) (h : p ≤ comap f q) : M ⧸ p →ₛₗ[τ₁₂] M₂ ⧸ q :=
  p.liftQ (q.mkQ.comp f) <| by simpa [ker_comp] using h

theorem mapQ_mkQ (f : M →ₛₗ[τ₁₂] M₂) {h} : (mapQ p q f h).comp p.mkQ = q.mkQ.comp f := by

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k] {X : Scheme.{u}}

section SecRes

variable (F G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k))

/-- Restriction of sections of a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site of a
scheme along an inclusion of opens, as a `k`-linear map. The public analogue of the
restriction operator used file-locally in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineVanishing`;
on the structure sheaf `X.moduleKSheaf k` it is `Scheme.resHom`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.secRes_moduleKSheaf`). -/
noncomputable def secRes {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
    F.obj.obj (op U) →ₗ[k] F.obj.obj (op V) :=
  (F.obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom

variable {F G}

@[simp]
lemma secRes_secRes {U V W : X.Opens} (h₁ : V ≤ U) (h₂ : W ≤ V) (s : F.obj.obj (op U)) :
    secRes F h₂ (secRes F h₁ s) = secRes F (h₂.trans h₁) s := by
  have hcomp : F.obj.map (homOfLE h₁).op ≫ F.obj.map (homOfLE h₂).op =
      F.obj.map (homOfLE (h₂.trans h₁)).op := by
    rw [← F.obj.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
  calc secRes F h₂ (secRes F h₁ s)
      = ((F.obj.map (homOfLE h₁).op ≫ F.obj.map (homOfLE h₂).op)).hom s := rfl
    _ = secRes F (h₂.trans h₁) s := by rw [hcomp]; rfl

/-- Restriction along `U ≤ U` is the identity (for an arbitrary proof, which is
proof-irrelevant). -/
@[simp]
lemma secRes_self {U : X.Opens} (h : U ≤ U) (s : F.obj.obj (op U)) : secRes F h s = s := by

of the line bundle on `U_j`.  Restriction to `U_i inter U_j` sends the equation-generated

overlap maps.  Their equalizer is the intrinsic theta restriction on the widened divisor.

theorem gluedQsmul_res {V W Z : X.Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (hVZ : V ≤ Z)

    24	finite projective over `R`, so the existing invertible-module transfer gives finite and

    12	/-!
    13	# The Θ-LAYER OVER A CHART-TYPED WIDENED COVER: a real absence, on an index that R2 empties
    14	
    15	> **READ `isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling` (below) BEFORE THIS DOCSTRING'S ARGUMENT.**
    16	> This module's original headline was "the widened carrier had no Θ-layer, and supplying it lets
    17	> cert-r2's producer reach U2". **The first clause is true; the second is refuted, in Lean, in
    18	> this file.** Every declaration here is indexed by a `ChartTyping C R π D`, and a cover with a
    19	> straddling piece admits *none* — which is exactly the case protection `I-0492`'s widening
    20	> exists to handle. So on those divisors every theorem below is vacuous, and the tree's only
    21	> `ChartTyping` producer is the migration *from* the old chart-typed carrier. Refutation and its
    22	> consequences: `isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling`; reviewer items `I-0779`/`I-0782`.
    23	>
    24	> What survives is worth keeping and is not the headline: the Θ-layer genuinely did not exist on
    25	> `AffAdaptation` (measurements below, independently confirmed as `I-0780`), it ports cleanly, and
    26	> it is now available for any cover that *does* carry a chart typing.
    27	
    28	Protection `I-0492` widened the certificate carrier to arbitrary affine opens, and the
    29	widened lane now produces a class from geometry
    30	(`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamZarAff_of_swallowing_affineOpen`,
    31	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffSeedGate.lean`).  That producer still cannot feed U2, and the
    32	reason recorded across five sessions — "U2 needs a certificate" — is **not** it.  The
    33	argument below correctly identifies the *absence*; where it overreaches is in treating
    34	supplying that absence as sufficient.
    35	
    36	## The measurement that renames the seam
    37	
    38	U2's consumer `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause` (`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean:121`)
    39	quantifies over `DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) π g`, the *chart-typed* value.  There is no
    40	map `DivFamZarAff → DivFamZar` and there cannot be (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2:
    41	a straddling divisor has no chart-typed certificate).  So the only usable route is to
    42	re-derive the ε-value facts on the widened carrier — and *that* is where the absence is:
    43	
    44	> `divFamEps_eq_of_le` (`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivQuot.lean`) needs projectivity and
    45	> constant rank `g` of the **window quotient**.  On `DivFam` those are landed
    46	> *unconditionally* (`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:106`/`:117`) — but their only proof
    47	> route is `windowQuotEquiv` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean:179`), whose target is
    48	> `A.ThetaGlued a`, and `ThetaGlued` / `thetaGluedEval` / `thetaOvlUnit` /
    49	> `thetaDeltaRight` / `ker_thetaGluedEval` are defined **only** on `DivisorAdaptation`
    50	> (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean`).
    51	
    52	Cross-measured at HEAD: of the files mentioning `AffAdaptation`, **zero** define any theta
    53	arrow.  `DivisorFamilyAffFraming.lean` is right that the ε-pair *statement* is
    54	carrier-indifferent (both carriers have the same `eqns` field and `divisorWindow` reads
    55	nothing else); the ε-pair **facts** are not, and statement was never separated from facts.
    56	
    57	## Why this is a port and not new mathematics
    58	
    59	The Θ-layer's chart-dependence is exactly **one `Bool` per piece**.  `FinCoverData`'s
    60	version reads it off the `Sum` index (`pieces_inl_le` / `pieces_inr_le`), which is why it
    61	looks chart-typed; but the side-uniform API it could have used already exists and is
    62	consumed by some sixty files:
    63	
    64	* `relThetaResSide` (`Picard/DivSchemeFamilySide.lean:155`) — the side component,
    65	  restricted into any open below `relPinnedChart (side j)`;
    66	* `relThetaSideUnit` (`:180`) — the matching unit of an ordered pair of sides, whose
    67	  four-case split *is* `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit`'s;
    68	* `relThetaResSide_matching` (`:194`) and `resHom_relThetaResSide` (`:172`).
    69	
    70	Each needs only `piece ≤ relPinnedChart (side j)` — which is **verbatim** the field
    71	`ChartTyping.piece_le` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:204`), the datum `I-0492`
    72	clause 3 deliberately kept *separate* from the certificate clauses precisely so the
    73	Θ-layer could have it without the certificate demanding it.
    74	
    75	So this file is the missing face, built the way clause 3 intends: the twisting data is
    76	indexed by a `ChartTyping`, and **no certificate clause and no locally-certified predicate
    77	mentions it**.
    78	
    79	## What this file does and does not claim
    80	
    81	It builds the widened Θ-twisted glued module and its evaluation, and proves the kernel
    82	bridge — left exactness, i.e. that the kernel is the *same* cover-independent vanishing
    83	submodule the chart-typed layer produces.  That is the input `windowQuotEquiv`'s widened
    84	analogue needs.
    85	
    86	It does **not** prove surjectivity of the widened evaluation (the right-exactness heart,
    87	`thetaGluedEval_surjective`'s analogue), and it does not produce a widened ε-value
    88	identity: those consume the widened certificate's (c2) clause through a widened
    89	`IsThetaPaired`, which is the next face and is *not* built here.  Read this as "the
    90	ε-value facts are now *stateable* over the widened carrier", not as a gate cleared.
    91	
    92	## Main declarations
    93	
    94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.thetaOvlUnit` — the twisting unit of an ordered pair of
    95	  widened pieces, read off a `ChartTyping` rather than a `Sum` index.
    96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.thetaGluedSubmodule` / `ThetaGlued` — the Θ-twisted
    97	  glued colength module over a widened cover, spelled as a kernel exactly as the
    98	  chart-typed one.
    99	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.thetaGluedEval` — the evaluation
   100	  `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}`.
   101	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.ker_thetaGluedEval` — **the kernel bridge**: the widened
   102	  kernel *is* the cover-independent vanishing submodule, hence literally the chart-typed
   103	  layer's kernel.
   104	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.windowCarve` / `ker_windowCarve` / `windowQuotEquiv` — the
   105	  bridge plugged in: the widened carve arrow's kernel is `divisorWindow d`, and (conditional on
   106	  surjectivity, which is **not** proved here) the quotient of the free window by it is the
   107	  widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`.  That last equivalence is the vehicle whose absence made the ε-value at a
   108	  `DivFamZarAff` unstateable.
   109	
   110	**A phrasing correction taken from a fresh-context review** (`I-0769`), because the wrong version
   111	was in this docstring: `ker_thetaGluedEval` does **not** show "`divisorWindow` is the same on both
   112	carriers" — `divisorWindow` takes only `d` and `hH1` and never mentioned a carrier, so that is
   113	vacuous.  The content runs the other way: *the widened evaluation's kernel lands on that
   114	already-fixed submodule.*
   115	-/

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once.    427	    rw [TwoLatticePair.range_diff_eq, himg]
   428	    trivial
   429	  obtain ⟨⟨x, y⟩, hxy⟩ := hn
   430	  rw [TwoLatticePair.diff_apply] at hxy
   431	  refine ⟨gluedToIdeal₀ A a le_rfl x, gluedToIdeal₁ A a le_rfl y,
   432	    fun z hz => germ_gluedToIdeal₀_mem le_rfl x z hz,
   433	    fun z hz => germ_gluedToIdeal₁_mem le_rfl y z hz, ?_⟩
   434	  -- read the splitting through the assemblies
   435	  have h0 := congrArg (gluedToIdeal₀ A a
   436	    (inf_le_left : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   437	      (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)) hxy
   438	  rw [gluedToIdeal₀_sub, gluedToIdeal₀_idealToGlued₀] at h0
   439	  -- the first summand: naturality of the chart-0 assembly
   440	  have h₀ : gluedToIdeal₀ A a
   441	      (inf_le_left : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   442	        (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
   443	      ((datumPair (A.thetaIdealDatum a)).ι₀ x)
   444	      = (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left (gluedToIdeal₀ A a le_rfl x) :=
   445	    gluedToIdeal₀_secRes inf_le_left le_rfl x
   446	  -- the second summand: the theta comparison and naturality of the chart-1 assembly
   447	  have h₁ : gluedToIdeal₀ A a
   448	      (inf_le_left : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   449	        (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
   450	      ((datumPair (A.thetaIdealDatum a)).ι₁ y)
   451	      = ((relThetaCocycle C R π a :
   452	          Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   453	            (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)ˣ) :
   454	          Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   455	            (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁))
   456	        * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (gluedToIdeal₁ A a le_rfl y) := by
   457	    have hcmp := gluedToIdeal₀_eq_theta_mul_gluedToIdeal₁
   458	      (le_rfl : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   459	        (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   460	          (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
   461	      (secRes ((A.thetaIdealDatum a).sheaf) inf_le_right y)
   462	    rw [Scheme.resHom_self,
   463	      gluedToIdeal₁_secRes inf_le_right le_rfl y] at hcmp
   464	    exact hcmp
   465	  rw [h₀, h₁] at h0

     9	# DD-4 (Task 4, right exactness) — the surjectivity assembly for `thetaGluedEval`
    10	
    11	The **assembly step** of the right exactness of the section sequence
    12	(`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §2.3 step 2): the Θ-twisted colength evaluation
    13	`thetaGluedEval : H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyTheta`
    14	is surjective, GIVEN the two cohomological inputs in section-level form:
    15	
    16	* **chart lifting** (`DivisorAdaptation.LiftsOnChart₀/₁`): every Θ-twisted glued colength
    17	  family lifts, on each pinned chart separately, to a chart section reducing to it on
    18	  every piece — the vanishing of `H¹` of the twisted ideal sheaf `𝒪(Θᵃ − d)` on the
    19	  affine pinned chart (Serre, quasi-coherent Čech on the basic-open pieces);
    20	* **overlap correction** (`relThetaOverlapCorrection`): every section of the chart
    21	  overlap all of whose germs lie in the stalk ideals of `d` splits as a Θ-twisted
    22	  difference of chart sections vanishing along `d` — the two-chart Čech
    23	  `H¹(𝒪(Θᵃ − d)) = 0` (relative; fired by the engine at fibre degree
    24	  `a·δ − deg d ≥ b`, DAT-0a).
    25	
    26	Given these, the preimage of a glued family `w` is assembled as follows: lift `w` on
    27	each chart (`σ₀`, `σ₁`), observe that the mismatch `τ = σ₀ − θᵃ·σ₁` on the chart overlap
    28	vanishes along `d` germwise (the Θ-twisted matching of `w` on the piece overlaps),
    29	correct by the overlap input (`τ = α₀ − θᵃ·α₁` with `αᵢ` vanishing along `d`), and check
    30	that `(σ₀ − α₀, σ₁ − α₁)` is a global twisted section evaluating to `w` — the correction
    31	disappears in every colength because a section vanishing along `d` germwise lies in the
    32	regular principal ideal `(f_j)` of each piece
    33	(`Scheme.mem_span_singleton_of_forall_germ`).
    34	
    35	The discharge of the two inputs from the glued-sheaf datum of `𝒪(Θᵃ − d)` and the rigid
    36	engine is the follow-on brick (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorThetaDatum`).
    37	-/

    64	  ∀ τ : Γ(relCurve C R,
    65	      (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁),

   154	/-- Every germ of an element of the overlap ideal `(f_i, f_j)` lies in the stalk ideal
   155	of `d`. -/
   156	lemma germ_mem_stalkIdeal_of_mem_ovlIdeal {i j : A.index}
   157	    {t : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)} (ht : t ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j)
   158	    (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :
   159	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hz).hom t
   160	      ∈ d.stalkIdeal z := by
   161	  obtain ⟨u, v, huv⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_pair.mp ht
   162	  have hgerm := congrArg
   163	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hz).hom huv
   164	  rw [map_add, map_mul, map_mul] at hgerm
   165	  rw [← hgerm]

   167	      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i))

   170	        (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i)
   171	          (A.eqn i))

   174	    rw [hswap, ← A.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal i hz.1]
   175	    exact Ideal.subset_span rfl
   176	  have hj : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hz).hom
   177	      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j))

   179	    have hswap : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hz).hom
   180	        (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j)
   181	          (A.eqn j))
   182	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz.2).hom (A.eqn j) :=

   184	    rw [hswap, ← A.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal j hz.2]

   188	/-! ## The assembly -/

   190	/-- **Right exactness of the section sequence, assembly form** (worksheet §2.3 step 2):
   191	given the chart-lifting inputs and the overlap-correction input, the Θ-twisted colength
   192	evaluation `thetaGluedEval : H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is surjective. -/
   193	theorem thetaGluedEval_surjective_of_liftsOnChart_of_correction
   194	    (hlift₀ : A.LiftsOnChart₀ a) (hlift₁ : A.LiftsOnChart₁ a)
   195	    (hcorr : relThetaOverlapCorrection π d a) :
   196	    Function.Surjective (A.thetaGluedEval a) := by
   197	  rintro ⟨w, hw⟩
   198	  obtain ⟨σ₀, hσ₀⟩ := hlift₀ w hw
   199	  obtain ⟨σ₁, hσ₁⟩ := hlift₁ w hw
   200	  -- the mismatch of the chart lifts on the chart overlap
   201	  obtain ⟨τ, hτdef⟩ : ∃ τ : Γ(relCurve C R,
   202	      (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁),
   203	      τ = (relCurve C R).resHom (le_inf le_top inf_le_left) σ₀
   204	        - ((relThetaCocycle C R π a :
   205	              Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   206	                (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)ˣ) :
   207	            Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   208	              (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁))
   209	          * (relCurve C R).resHom (le_inf le_top inf_le_right) σ₁ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
   210	  -- the mismatch vanishes along `d` germwise: read the Θ-twisted matching of `w`
   211	  -- on a piece overlap through each point
   212	  have hτ : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   213	      (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁),
   214	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ _ z hz).hom τ ∈ d.stalkIdeal z := by
   215	    intro z hz
   216	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.cover₀ hz.1)
   217	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.cover₁ hz.2)
   218	    have hzij : z ∈ A.pieces (Sum.inl i) ⊓ A.pieces (Sum.inr j) := ⟨hi, hj⟩
   219	    -- the Θ-twisted matching of `w` at the pair `(inl i, inr j)`,
   220	    -- as a membership in the overlap ideal
   221	    have hmatch := (A.mem_thetaGluedSubmodule_iff a w).mp hw (Sum.inl i, Sum.inr j)
   222	    dsimp only at hmatch
   223	    rw [← hσ₀ i, ← hσ₁ j, toOvlLeft_mk, toOvlRight_mk,
   224	      FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_inl_inr, Scheme.resHom_resHom, Scheme.resHom_resHom,
   225	      ← map_mul, ← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem] at hmatch
   226	    have hker := germ_mem_stalkIdeal_of_mem_ovlIdeal hmatch z hzij
   227	    rw [map_sub, map_mul] at hker
   228	    -- collapse germs of restrictions to germs of the ambient sections

   230	        (A.pieces (Sum.inl i) ⊓ A.pieces (Sum.inr j)) z hzij).hom
   231	        ((relCurve C R).resHom
   232	          (((inf_le_left : A.pieces (Sum.inl i) ⊓ A.pieces (Sum.inr j)
   233	              ≤ A.pieces (Sum.inl i))).trans (le_inf le_top (A.pieces_inl_le i))) σ₀)
   234	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   235	            (⊤ ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀) z
   236	            ⟨trivial, hz.1⟩).hom σ₀ :=
   237	      TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _
   238	    have hswap₁ : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   239	        (A.pieces (Sum.inl i) ⊓ A.pieces (Sum.inr j)) z hzij).hom
   240	        ((relCurve C R).resHom
   241	          (((inf_le_right : A.pieces (Sum.inl i) ⊓ A.pieces (Sum.inr j)
   242	              ≤ A.pieces (Sum.inr j))).trans (le_inf le_top (A.pieces_inr_le j))) σ₁)
   243	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   244	            (⊤ ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁) z
   245	            ⟨trivial, hz.2⟩).hom σ₁ :=
   246	      TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _
   247	    have hswapθ : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   248	        (A.pieces (Sum.inl i) ⊓ A.pieces (Sum.inr j)) z hzij).hom
   249	        (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict
   250	            (inf_le_inf (A.pieces_inl_le i) (A.pieces_inr_le j))
